To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• Graph of words (GOW) is a more discriminative representation of documents than the traditional bag-of-words representation.

(1) the graph-of-words representation of textual data is a promising alternative to the traditional bag-of-words representation for text categorization; and (2) by using frequent subgraph mining, we can extract long-distance n-gram features from the graph-of- words representation that are more discriminative than those obtained from the bag-of-words model.

(i) text categorization as graph classification problem outperforms baseline approaches in terms of accuracy and macro-avereaged F1-score; (ii) frequent subgraph mining is a powerful feature extraction method that is able to extract more discriminative information from the graph-of-words representation; (iii) k-core decomposition is a powerful tool that can be used to reduce the graph-of-works representation without any cost in prediction performances, thus speeding up the feature extration step.
